### Section 2: Founding Charter and Mission Statement

The Network was established under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, with the primary objective of providing emergency shelter, comprehensive care, and rehabilitation support to vulnerable populations including, but not limited to, homeless individuals, displaced families, and persons affected by natural or man-made disasters.

**Mission Statement (as adopted 2008-04-01):** To provide dignified, safe, and accessible emergency shelter and allied support services to individuals and families in crisis, operating with transparency, accountability, and a commitment to the highest standards of care.

- Human dignity and non-discrimination in all service delivery
- Community participation and stakeholder engagement
- Evidence-based program design and continuous quality improvement
- Environmental sustainability in shelter operations

**CIRCULAR NO. ASN/ADMN/2014/07**

**Date of Issue:** 2014-03-15
**Effective Date:** 2014-04-01
**Supersedes:** Circular No. ASN/ADMN/2012/03 (dated 2012-02-10)

**Subject: Revised Standard Operating Procedures for Emergency Shelter Operations**

The Governing Council, at its meeting held on 2014-02-28, approved revisions to the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) governing the emergency shelter operations of the Network. These revisions are intended to streamline response protocols, clarify reporting hierarchies, and align our practices with the updated guidelines issued by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

All Shelter Managers, Head Counsellors, and staff members are required to familiarise themselves with the contents of this circular. The revised SOPs shall come into force with effect from 2014-04-01. Any operational procedures that conflict with the provisions herein stand superseded from that date.

**Key Revisions:**

1. **Intake and Registration:** All beneficiaries seeking shelter shall be registered within 2 hours of arrival. The registration form (Form ASN-01) must be completed in duplicate, with one copy retained at the shelter and one forwarded to the National Operations Coordinator's office within 24 hours.

2. **Emergency Bed Allocation:** In the event of a medical emergency, the Shelter Manager is authorised to allocate beds on a priority basis without awaiting approval from the central office. A report of such allocation must be submitted to the National Operations Coordinator within 6 hours of the allocation.

3. **Incident Reporting:** All incidents, including but not limited to medical emergencies, altercations, and property damage, must be reported to the central office using Form ASN-04. The report must be submitted within 12 hours of the incident. For incidents of a critical nature, an immediate telephonic notification to the National Operations Coordinator is mandatory, followed by the written report within the stipulated timeframe.

4. **Staff Duty Schedules:** Duty rosters for all shelter staff shall be prepared on a monthly basis and displayed on the notice board by the 25th of the preceding month. Any changes to the roster must be communicated to the affected staff members at least 48 hours in advance.

5. **Inventory Management:** Shelters are required to maintain a minimum stock of essential supplies, including food grains, medicines, and bedding. The minimum stock levels are specified in Annexure A of the revised SOPs. Stock levels shall be reviewed on the first working day of every month.

6. **Coordination with Local Authorities:** Shelter Managers are directed to establish and maintain a liaison with the local police station, municipal corporation, and nearest government hospital. A list of contact numbers shall be updated quarterly and displayed near the main entrance of each shelter.

The complete text of the revised SOPs is available in the central records office and has been circulated to all shelters in electronic format.

**1. Introduction**

The Aarogya Shelter Network completed its sixteenth year of operation during the period under review (1 April 2023 to 31 March 2024). This report summarises the activities, achievements, and challenges of the Network across its fourteen shelters in four states. The report has been prepared in accordance with the reporting guidelines issued under Circular No. ASN/ADMN/2014/07, as amended.

The year witnessed a consolidation of our outreach services, a significant expansion of the vocational training programme, and the successful completion of the retrofitting works at the Bhopal and Lucknow shelters. The Governing Council expresses its gratitude to all partner agencies, donors, and staff whose contributions made these achievements possible.

---

**2. Key Statistics at a Glance**

| Indicator | 2022–23 | 2023–24 | Change |
|-----------|---------|---------|--------|
| Total beneficiaries served | 4,820 | 5,310 | +10.2% |
| Average daily occupancy (all shelters) | 1,240 | 1,385 | +11.7% |
| Shelter utilisation rate | 78% | 83% | +5 pts |
| Meals served | 412,000 | 458,700 | +11.3% |
| Medical consultations | 9,860 | 11,240 | +14.0% |
| Vocational training completions | 310 | 415 | +33.9% |
| Successful family reunifications | 96 | 118 | +22.9% |

The utilisation rate is computed as the ratio of occupied bed-nights to total available bed-nights, excluding beds reserved for emergency overflow. The figures include all fourteen shelters operating as of 31 March 2024.

---

**3. Shelter Operations**

**3.1 Capacity and Occupancy**

As of 31 March 2024, the Network operated a combined capacity of 1,670 beds. The Delhi Central Shelter (500 beds) and the Mumbai Harbour Shelter (350 beds) remain the largest facilities. The new Nagpur Shelter, which opened in October 2023, contributed 120 beds and achieved an average utilisation of 71% within its first six months of operation.

Seasonal pressure was most acute during the winter months (December to February) in the northern shelters. The Delhi Central Shelter operated at full capacity for 61 consecutive nights during this period. Overflow arrangements with partner NGOs were activated on 23 occasions, compared to 17 in the previous year.

**3.2 Intake and Registration**

A total of 7,240 new admissions were processed during the year. The average time from arrival to registration completion was 42 minutes, within the 24-hour reporting standard. All admissions were registered in the central digital registry within the stipulated timeframe. The average length of stay was 34 days, with a median of 21 days.

**3.3 Staffing**

The Network employed 412 staff members as of 31 March 2024, including shelter managers, counsellors, nurses, security personnel, and support staff. Staff turnover was 18%, a slight reduction from the previous year's 21%. The retention of trained counsellors remains a priority, and a revised pay scale was approved by the Governing Council in September 2023.

---

**4. Health and Medical Services**

**4.1 Medical Camps**

A total of 48 medical camps were organised across all shelters, in collaboration with government district hospitals and private medical colleges. These camps provided 11,240 consultations, including general health check-ups, immunisations, and mental health screenings.

**4.2 Referrals**

A total of 1,340 beneficiaries were referred to government hospitals for inpatient care or specialist consultation. The referral protocol, revised in 2022, was followed in all cases. The average time from referral to admission was 18 hours, with urgent cases prioritised.

**4.3 Mental Health Support**

The Network employed 12 full-time counsellors and 6 visiting psychiatrists. A total of 2,180 individual counselling sessions and 190 group therapy sessions were conducted. The tele-counselling helpline, launched in January 2023, received 1,540 calls during the year, with an average response time of 8 minutes.

# Aarogya Shelter Network
## Official Records and Historical Overview

### Section 1: Network Registration and Commencement of Operations

**Registered Entity Name:** Aarogya Shelter Network (hereafter referred to as "ASN" or "the Network")

**Date of Registration:** 15 January 2008
**Certificate Number:** NGO/2008/DEL/1147
**Registered Office Address:** 42, Community Services Block, Lajpat Nagar II, New Delhi – 110024

**Commencement of Operations:** According to the official records, Aarogya Shelter Network has been operating since 2008-04-01. Record status: current. The founding board convened its inaugural meeting on 12 March 2008 at the registered office, during which the Articles of Association were adopted and the initial Governing Council was constituted. The commencement date of 1 April 2008 marks the formal start of all service delivery activities, and this date remains the operative reference for all anniversaries, statutory filings, and operational audits undertaken by the Network.

### Section 2: Founding Charter and Mission Statement

The Network was established under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, with the primary objective of providing emergency shelter, comprehensive care, and rehabilitation support to vulnerable populations including, but not limited to, homeless individuals, displaced families, and persons affected by natural or man-made disasters.

**Mission Statement (as adopted 2008-04-01):** To provide dignified, safe, and accessible emergency shelter and allied support services to individuals and families in crisis, operating with transparency, accountability, and a commitment to the highest standards of care.

**Core Values:**
- Human dignity and non-discrimination in all service delivery
- Community participation and stakeholder engagement
- Evidence-based program design and continuous quality improvement
- Environmental sustainability in shelter operations

**Subject: Revised Standard Operating Procedures for Emergency Shelter Operations**

The Governing Council, at its meeting held on 2014-02-28, approved revisions to the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) governing the emergency shelter operations of the Network. These revisions are intended to streamline response protocols, clarify reporting hierarchies, and align our practices with the updated guidelines issued by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

All Shelter Managers, Head Counsellors, and staff members are required to familiarise themselves with the contents of this circular. The revised SOPs shall come into force with effect from 2014-04-01. Any operational procedures that conflict with the provisions herein stand superseded from that date.

**Key Revisions:**

1. **Intake and Registration:** All beneficiaries seeking shelter shall be registered within 2 hours of arrival. The registration form (Form ASN-01) must be completed in duplicate, with one copy retained at the shelter and one forwarded to the National Operations Coordinator's office within 24 hours.

2. **Emergency Bed Allocation:** In the event of a medical emergency, the Shelter Manager is authorised to allocate beds on a priority basis without awaiting approval from the central office. A report of such allocation must be submitted to the National Operations Coordinator within 6 hours of the allocation.

3. **Incident Reporting:** All incidents, including but not limited to medical emergencies, altercations, and property damage, must be reported to the central office using Form ASN-04. The report must be submitted within 12 hours of the incident. For incidents of a critical nature, an immediate telephonic notification to the National Operations Coordinator is mandatory, followed by the written report within the stipulated timeframe.

4. **Staff Duty Schedules:** Duty rosters for all shelter staff shall be prepared on a monthly basis and displayed on the notice board by the 25th of the preceding month. Any changes to the roster must be communicated to the affected staff members at least 48 hours in advance.

5. **Inventory Management:** Shelters are required to maintain a minimum stock of essential supplies, including food grains, medicines, and bedding. The minimum stock levels are specified in Annexure A of the revised SOPs. Stock levels shall be reviewed on the first working day of every month.

6. **Coordination with Local Authorities:** Shelter Managers are directed to establish and maintain a liaison with the local police station, municipal corporation, and nearest government hospital. A list of contact numbers shall be updated quarterly and displayed near the main entrance of each shelter.

The complete text of the revised SOPs is available in the central records office and has been circulated to all shelters in electronic format.

**AAROGYA SHELTER NETWORK**
**ANNUAL REPORT 2023–24**
**Submitted to the Governing Council and Partner Agencies**
**Report No. ASN/AR/2024/02**
**Date of Issue: 2024-06-15**

---

**1. Introduction**

The Aarogya Shelter Network completed its sixteenth year of operation during the period under review (1 April 2023 to 31 March 2024). This report summarises the activities, achievements, and challenges of the Network across its fourteen shelters in four states. The report has been prepared in accordance with the reporting guidelines issued under Circular No. ASN/ADMN/2014/07, as amended.

The year witnessed a consolidation of our outreach services, a significant expansion of the vocational training programme, and the successful completion of the retrofitting works at the Bhopal and Lucknow shelters. The Governing Council expresses its gratitude to all partner agencies, donors, and staff whose contributions made these achievements possible.

---

**2. Key Statistics at a Glance**

| Indicator | 2022–23 | 2023–24 | Change |
|-----------|---------|---------|--------|
| Total beneficiaries served | 4,820 | 5,310 | +10.2% |
| Average daily occupancy (all shelters) | 1,240 | 1,385 | +11.7% |
| Shelter utilisation rate | 78% | 83% | +5 pts |
| Meals served | 412,000 | 458,700 | +11.3% |
| Medical consultations | 9,860 | 11,240 | +14.0% |
| Vocational training completions | 310 | 415 | +33.9% |
| Successful family reunifications | 96 | 118 | +22.9% |

The utilisation rate is computed as the ratio of occupied bed-nights to total available bed-nights, excluding beds reserved for emergency overflow. The figures include all fourteen shelters operating as of 31 March 2024.

---

**3. Shelter Operations**

**3.1 Capacity and Occupancy**

As of 31 March 2024, the Network operated a combined capacity of 1,670 beds. The Delhi Central Shelter (500 beds) and the Mumbai Harbour Shelter (350 beds) remain the largest facilities. The new Nagpur Shelter, which opened in October 2023, contributed 120 beds and achieved an average utilisation of 71% within its first six months of operation.

Seasonal pressure was most acute during the winter months (December to February) in the northern shelters. The Delhi Central Shelter operated at full capacity for 61 consecutive nights during this period. Overflow arrangements with partner NGOs were activated on 23 occasions, compared to 17 in the previous year.

**3.2 Intake and Registration**

A total of 7,240 new admissions were processed during the year. The average time from arrival to registration completion was 42 minutes, within the 24-hour reporting standard. All admissions were registered in the central digital registry within the stipulated timeframe. The average length of stay was 34 days, with a median of 21 days.

**3.3 Staffing**

The Network employed 412 staff members as of 31 March 2024, including shelter managers, counsellors, nurses, security personnel, and support staff. Staff turnover was 18%, a slight reduction from the previous year's 21%. The retention of trained counsellors remains a priority, and a revised pay scale was approved by the Governing Council in September 2023.

---

**4. Health and Medical Services**

**4.1 Medical Camps**

A total of 48 medical camps were organised across all shelters, in collaboration with government district hospitals and private medical colleges. These camps provided 11,240 consultations, including general health check-ups, immunisations, and mental health screenings.

**4.2 Referrals**

A total of 1,340 beneficiaries were referred to government hospitals for inpatient care or specialist consultation. The referral protocol, revised in 2022, was followed in all cases. The average time from referral to admission was 18 hours, with urgent cases prioritised.

**4.3 Mental Health Support**

The Network employed 12 full-time counsellors and 6 visiting psychiatrists. A total of 2,180 individual counselling sessions and 190 group therapy sessions were conducted. The tele-counselling helpline, launched in January 2023, received 1,540 calls during the year, with an average response time of 8 minutes.

**5. Incident Reports and Safety Issues**

The following incidents were reported and logged during September. Each entry includes the date, time, ward, description, action taken, and current status.

**Incident ID: INC-2024-0912**
- **Date/Time:** 12-Sep, 14:30 IST
- **Location:** Ward C, near the structural repair zone
- **Reported By:** Security Guard (M. Ansari)
- **Description:** A loose electrical wire was found hanging from the ceiling near the repair area. The wire was live and posed a risk to residents and workers.
- **Immediate Action:** The area was cordoned off. The electrician on duty was called and the power supply to that section was switched off at 14:40 IST.
- **Root Cause (Preliminary):** The wire was dislodged during the ongoing structural repair work in Ward C.
- **Corrective Action:** The wire was properly insulated and re-fixed on the same day at 16:10 IST. A review of all exposed wiring in the repair zone was completed on 13-Sep.
- **Current Status:** Closed. No injury reported. The incident was discussed in the weekly safety meeting on 16-Sep.

**Incident ID: INC-2024-0918**
- **Date/Time:** 18-Sep, 21:45 IST
- **Location:** Main dining hall
- **Reported By:** Volunteer (K. Devi)
- **Description:** A minor slip-and-fall incident. A resident (elderly male, approx. 65 yrs) slipped on a wet floor near the water cooler. He was helped up immediately by two nearby residents.
- **Immediate Action:** First aid was provided. The resident did not complain of pain at the time. The floor was wiped and a caution sign was placed.
- **Follow-up:** The resident was observed by the visiting nurse on 19-Sep morning. No swelling or bruising was noted. He was advised to use the handrail in the future.
- **Current Status:** Closed. No medical referral required.

**Incident ID: INC-2024-0922**
- **Date/Time:** 22-Sep, 11:10 IST
- **Location:** Ward A, Bed 45
- **Reported By:** Nurse (P. Singh)
- **Description:** A resident reported a skin rash. On examination, the nurse suspected scabies. The resident had been in the shelter since 02-Aug.
- **Immediate Action:** The resident was isolated in a separate room. A doctor was called and the diagnosis was confirmed on 23-Sep.
- **Corrective Action:** The affected bed was stripped, and the linen was washed in hot water with disinfectant. The mattress was treated with a permethrin spray. All residents in Ward A were asked to report any itching.
- **Follow-up:** Two more cases were identified on 25-Sep in Ward A. All three residents are under treatment. A second round of mattress treatment was done on 27-Sep.
- **Current Status:** Open. Monitoring continues. No new cases reported since 27-Sep.

The following section consolidates the compliance status of all shelter operations against the Aarogya Shelter Network Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Government of Maharashtra directives. Incident report filed with the Medical Officer. **Status: Closed** (verified 14-Aug).
- **Finding (02-Sep):** SH-06 fire exit door on the ground floor was found blocked by stored mattresses during a surprise check. **Action:** Mattresses moved to designated storage; staff briefing conducted on 03-Sep. **Status: Closed** (verified 04-Sep).
- **Finding (21-Sep):** The visitor entry register at SH-01 had three missing signature columns for 19-Sep evening hours. **Action:** Security personnel counseled; register format updated to include time-out column. **Status: Closed** (verified 25-Sep).

- **Resident Capacity Policy (Rev 4, 2024):** The policy mandates that total occupancy shall not exceed 95% of sanctioned capacity at any time, to maintain emergency buffer beds.
